key_insight: The paper proposes “alignment plausibility” as a new standard for showing that AI systems in healthcare are designed, trained, and supervised in ways that support safe outcomes.
clinical_relevance: For mental health and other health uses of LLMs, it offers a framework for reducing harms like dependency, boundary erosion, and reinforcement of distorted beliefs.
method: Define clinical values explicitly before model development
Train the model so those values are embedded in behavior
Monitor deployment for drift and longer-term harms, similar to clinical supervision
evidence_signal: This is a conceptual/regulatory proposal drawn from analogy to clinical safety and biological plausibility rather than from new empirical data in the abstract.
watch_item: A key challenge is proving that values, training, and oversight are consistently implemented and effective across real-world deployment, not just specified in policy.
paper_title: Alignment Plausibility: A New Standard for Assuring AI in Healthcare
